doc.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999

title: Sitting in with Uncle Phil at Nick's and taking the job
summary: Marty played Dixieland with Phil at Nick's, surprised him with a bop solo, and got the job.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well as time passed, eventually you got to work with your uncle?

Yes, my Uncle Phil. And that’s a funny story too, because he had really a great Dixieland band, and I couldn’t play Dixieland one, not one note. So my brother-in-law, Shorty Allen, the piano player, he’s married to my sister, and the four of us and somebody else, I forget who was with us, we went to New York to see “Some Like it Hot.” And when we came out we said let’s go see Uncle Phil at Nick’s. He was working at Nick’s. So we go to see him at Nick’s. Now Phil, he knew that Shorty and I were like considered bebop piano players, because we didn’t know from Dixieland. So he felt so funny because he said, “Either one of you guys want to sit in?” Hoping we’d say no, no, we can’t play that kind of music. So I said, “Shorty, go ahead, why don’t you play.” So Shorty says, “Okay.” So he went and sat in and played, and the next set Phil says now I’ve got to ask my nephew, right. Marty you want to sit in? I said, yeah, all right, okay. So I sat and he says, “what do you want to play?” I says, “Phil, I don’t know your routines, your songs, your repertoire.” I said, “pick a song.” He says, “How about ‘Back Home Again in Indiana.’” I said bing — I know that one. So we started playing “Back Home Again in Indiana” and luckily he played it [scats] not too fast, see it was like slow. Which means when it got to my solo, when I took a piano solo, just because I was in Rome I figured let me do this, and he turns around at me and he says oh yeah? Because I’m figuring well I’ve got to make the guy happy anyway. So I’m going [scats] and he turned around and he’s slapping the piano like this. So when we finished the set he comes over to me and he says, “Marty come over here I’m going to talk to you.” I knew right away what he was going to say see? And I was going to say yes, because I wanted to learn how to play some Dixieland. Sure enough he took me in the corner and he says, “I didn’t know you could play like that.” I says, “I don’t.” He said, “well I just heard you.” I said, “Phil, that was for you,” because I didn’t want you to say bebop piano players see? So I said, “I think I would like that.” So I took the band — I took the job with the band. That’s how I wound up with his band.
The Memphis Five was it called?
